# Plan Review Cycle

Radice del plugin: `/home/bench/bench-run-config/plugins/cache/maat/maat/1.6.0`. Nei file di questa skill che leggi con Read, `/home/bench/bench-run-config/plugins/cache/maat/maat/1.6.0` vale questo percorso: sostituiscilo prima di eseguire un comando.

Prima di ogni comando Bash o PowerShell, scrivi `description` secondo `/home/bench/bench-run-config/plugins/cache/maat/maat/1.6.0/docs/descrizione-comandi.md`.

You orchestrate a bounded planning and adversarial review workflow: a plan inside the spec file, reviewed by
the local `spec-plan-reviewer` agent until approved, a stop condition, or the budget. Do not implement code.
Where the rest lives — read a file only when this one sends you there:
- `autore.md` — how the plan is written and revised (plan shape, format 2, test level, floors): read by you at
  Step 1, and by the fresh author sub-agent of each format-2 revision;
- `revisori.md` — the reviewers' mandates: read by the reviewer agent itself;
- `formato-1.md` — a re-opened plan with no `Plan format: 2` line: read it only then;
- `plan-check.sh` — the code: structure, boundaries, differences, decisions (below). What moved out of this file
  into code, with its test: `/home/bench/bench-run-config/plugins/cache/maat/maat/1.6.0/skills/full-implementation-cycle/riferimento.md`, «Rules in code».

.claude/.ai-workflow/spec-split-parser-modules.md

## Single writable artifact

- You write only `.claude/.ai-workflow/spec-<name>.md`, and in it only `## Implementation plan` with its
  `### Plan review changelog`: never the spec sections above, never `## Implementation review`.
- The status lines (`Plan format: 2`, `Plan status:`, `Test level:`, `Risk surfaces:`, `Approved basis:`)
  are line-anchored and single-occurrence; prose and the changelog never reproduce those prefixes.
- **Languages (Maat 1.3.0)**: write the English headings and keywords (autore.md, «Languages»); every reader also
  accepts the Italian ones of older specs (`## Piano di implementazione`, `### Changelog revisione piano`,
  `Superfici a rischio:`…). A section that already exists keeps its heading: English only for a section created
  new, never both (`lint` VIOLAZIONE). An approved plan is never translated.
- **An approved plan is never edited**: only its changelog (notes, metric line). Any other change is a
  re-opening (below); `Approved basis:` makes a hand edit visible (`basis` → `STALE`, and the cycle stops).

## plan-check.sh — the code

`bash "/home/bench/bench-run-config/plugins/cache/maat/maat/1.6.0/scripts/plan-check.sh" <cmd> …` — exit 0 ok · 1 `VIOLAZIONE` · 2 usage; an
`AVVISO` never changes the exit. A `VIOLAZIONE` is fixed before a reviewer sees the plan.
The keywords (`VIOLAZIONE`, `AVVISO`, `ERRORE DURO`, `Percorso:`, `Scheletro:`, `S2:`) are the same in every language;
the explanation after them follows `lingua` of `.claude/maat.json` (Maat 1.4.0).

| command | what it decides |
|---|---|
| `lint <spec> [--baseline <copy>]` | status lines, sections above untouched, surfaces and floors — before every round |
| `lint2 <spec>` | format 2: requirements ↔ tests ↔ steps ↔ files, blocks, test table and mutations, removed strings still asserted, Python test ids (`::`), reds that need a stub in an existing file; AVVISO for a module without `report` |
| `skeleton <spec>` | the size gate (skeleton and full plan); `Split: rejected` (or `Taglio: rifiutato`) in the spec → exit 0 |
| `split <mother> <child…>` | a cut: every requirement in exactly one child, `Depends on:` / `Interface for:` (or `Dipende da:` / `Interfaccia per:`) present |
| `route <spec>` | format 2 branch: `Percorso: leggero \| pieno — <motivo>` |
| `delta <copy> <spec>` | the `range:` lines rewritten since the copy, plus `xref:` lines; empty or whole-file → exit 1: that round runs at full scope |
| `s2 <spec> --delta <f> --gate <f> [--respinti <n>]` | `S2: APPROVA \| CORREGGI \| RILANCIA \| IMPRONTA DIVERSA \| STOP` |
| `basis <spec>` · `gen <spec>` | the fingerprint to record at approval · the downstream procedure (format 2) |

## `<name>`, container, re-opening

- A spec path → basename without `spec-`, normalised to `[a-z0-9._-]`. Pasted text → a kebab-case slug of its
  first heading (none → ask now) and the container, the text as `## Context` and `## Functional requirements`. No
  timestamps, no suffixes: an existing file is refined in place.
- **Re-opening an approved plan** (the only legal amendment): copy the spec to the scratchpad first (the delta
  baseline); new requirements are written above by the user or `spec-author`, never by you; `Plan status:
  DRAFT`, plus any missing status line (and a floor or `⚠️` line for a declared critical surface); the amendment
  as surgical edits, recorded in the changelog; then straight to the delta round, fresh budget. Format 1 →
  `formato-1.md`.

Run the whole cycle in one uninterrupted turn: no pause and no confirmation between steps, rounds, revisions.

## Budget and stops

**4 iterations** (format 2; format 1: `formato-1.md`): one fan-out, one S2 pair, one fresh-eyes run = one
iteration. At the budget without approval → `Plan status: NEEDS HUMAN DECISION`. Other stops, also →
`NEEDS HUMAN DECISION`: a `STOP_HUMAN_DECISION_REQUIRED` from any reviewer · a recurrence · a rejected finding
re-raised by the same producer with no new evidence (disagreement on a verifiable fact) · scope not in the spec
· an ambiguity the codebase cannot resolve · `skeleton` exit 1 (the cut proposal, Step 1).

## Findings

- Only `blocker`/`major` block, and only with a **verifiable anchor**: `code` (`path:line` that says it) ·
  `spec/plan` (a line contradicting or omitting something checkable) · `absence` (pattern + scope + 0 results) ·
  `measure` (a result of the declared remote verification you supplied). No anchor → optional.
- **Verify before applying**: 1 Read or 1 Grep on the anchor (real data: a read-only query of the remote verification, not under
  `--no-dev`). Reject **only if the anchor is literally false**, never on reasoning — you own the plan. A
  rejection: one changelog line `rifiutato: <key> — <refutation>`, the «Rejected» list of every later prompt and
  of the final response; it does not count toward recurrence.
- `minor`/`nit` are **never applied**, not even after approval: one changelog line each, notes for the
  implementer. A finding needed for correctness is a `major`.
- **One round, several reviewers**: a `STOP_HUMAN_DECISION_REQUIRED` dominates; one `NEEDS_CHANGES` makes the
  round `NEEDS_CHANGES`; `APPROVED` only if all approve.
- **A partial review is not an approval**: an `APPROVED` with `Blocked on:` or uncovered ranges → re-run that
  producer on those ranges, free once per producer and range; a second partial there costs an iteration, a
  third is `STOP_HUMAN_DECISION_REQUIRED`.
- **Recurrence is yours** (the reviewers are stateless): a table `key → state`, never the full reviews; key
  `<area>/<claim in 5 words>` plus its anchored symbol or path, never a line number; states `aperto · risolto ·
  rifiutato · reintrodotto`. The same blocker/major in two consecutive runs of the same producer →
  `STOP_HUMAN_DECISION_REQUIRED`; `reintrodotto` (a `risolto` key back after a later edit) is a label, not a stop.

## Step 1: the plan

Level: `--tests=min|std|full` (aliases «test minimi», «solo i gate» → `min`; «test completi», «tutti i test» →
`full`), default `std`. You write the plan yourself: read `/home/bench/bench-run-config/plugins/cache/maat/maat/1.6.0/skills/plan-review-cycle/autore.md` now and
follow it. Copy the spec to the scratchpad (the `lint` baseline), write the **skeleton** only, then `skeleton`:
- `SOTTO IL TETTO` → write the full plan from the skeleton; then `lint --baseline`,
  `lint2`, `skeleton` again (the full-plan ceiling), `route`, and refresh the context pack
  (`bash "/home/bench/bench-run-config/plugins/cache/maat/maat/1.6.0/scripts/context-pack.sh" <spec>`: the plan changed the spec's fingerprint);
- `SOPRA IL TETTO` → **cut proposal**: `maat:spec-author` in mode `split` (Task) with the spec path and the `skeleton`
  output; `split <spec> <children…>`; a `VIOLAZIONE` goes back to `maat:spec-author` once, again → report it. Then
  `Plan status: NEEDS HUMAN DECISION`, changelog note «scheletro sopra il tetto: proposta di taglio in N
  anelli», and stop with the proposal: the rings in order, their requirements, what users see between rings.
  The user decides once; a rejection is recorded above the plan by `spec-author` (`Split: rejected —
  <date>`; `Taglio: rifiutato` in an older spec), and from then on `skeleton` lets the single plan go on.

**Branch.** `--full` always wins. Otherwise `route`: `Percorso: leggero` → the rounds of
`plan-review-cycle-light`; `pieno` → Step 2 (`--light` is honoured only with `leggero`). Say it in one line.

## Step 2: round 1 — three lenses in one message

Three `maat:spec-plan-reviewer` agents in a single message, each: «Use the maat:spec-plan-reviewer agent. Read
`/home/bench/bench-run-config/plugins/cache/maat/maat/1.6.0/skills/plan-review-cycle/revisori.md`, section «Round 1», and follow it. Lens: <L1|L2|L3>. Spec + plan
file: <path>. Ranges: spec <offset/limit>, plan <offset/limit>. Context pack: <path | none>. Test level: <lvl>.
Risk surfaces: <tokens>.» Aggregate. `APPROVED` outright → Step 3, but first one fresh-eyes reviewer
alone when a critical surface (`permissions`, `data`, `destructive` — `permessi`, `dati`, `distruttiva`) is declared.

## S2: revise, then delta ∥ fresh eyes (every later round)

1. Verify each blocker/major. Copy the spec to the scratchpad, then — **the author is fresh at every round**, you
   keep the finding table and the recurrence — an author sub-agent (Task): the spec path, the
   findings to apply with their verified anchors, «read `autore.md`, section «How to revise», apply only these».
   Then `lint --baseline`, `lint2`, `delta <copy> <spec>`. All findings rejected → no author, no delta: step 2.
2. One message, two `maat:spec-plan-reviewer` agents on the same plan — «read `revisori.md`, section «Delta»» and
   «… section «Fresh eyes»» — with: the `range:` and `xref:` lines, the pertinent requirement ranges, level and
   surfaces (every round), resolved findings (key + symbol + one line), rejected ones (key + refutation), test
   cases removed as over-testing, budget ~20 → 15 → 12. Save each reply to the scratchpad with, as first line,
   `Impronta piano: <plan value of basis at launch>`.
3. `s2 <spec> --delta <f> --gate <f> --respinti <n>` (`n` = the blocker/major of **these two** replies you
   rejected): `APPROVA` → Step 3 · `CORREGGI` → next round · `RILANCIA` → both again, together, with the
   rejected list · `IMPRONTA DIVERSA` → relaunch on the current plan · `STOP` → `NEEDS HUMAN DECISION`.

## Step 3: decide

- **Approved** → `Plan status: APPROVED`; `basis <spec>` and its whole `Basis:` value as `Approved basis: <value>`
  right under `Risk surfaces:` (or `Superfici a rischio:`) (replacing an older one; a ring's `madre`/`prec`/`interfaccia` included);
  `basis` again must say `FRESH`; format 2: `gen <spec>` must exit 0. Never write ` · tests <fp>`: the test-red
  phase does. Then, in the changelog only, the optional findings as notes and the metric line.
- **Not approved** (budget, stop) → `Plan status: NEEDS HUMAN DECISION`, the open decision, the metric line.

The **metric line**, last line of the changelog (no backticks, never the status prefixes; one per run of the
cycle): `Metrica ciclo: giri=5 · R1=2/3 · delta=1/2 · gate=0/1 · rifiutati=1 · ricorrenze=0 · reintrodotti=1 ·
esito=approvato · livello=std · superfici=permessi,dati · formato=2` (`R1`/`delta`/`gate` = blocker/major found
in that phase over its runs; `giri` = iterations).

## Final response

`Decision:` · the spec file · `Plan status:` · summary · unresolved blocker/major · rejected findings (key +
refutation) · optional findings, not applied · `Test level: <lvl> (<default std | esplicito | alias>)` ·
`Risk surfaces:` with the floor of each critical surface (or its `⚠️`) · next command: approved →
`/maat:implementation-review-cycle <name>`, saying plainly that **plan approval does not replace the code review**
(the quick `--light` round after implementing is always worth it); not approved → the human decision needed. A
`/browser-qa` suggestion only when the plan changes a multi-step UI journey or wires UI state to persistence with
no component test — for the human, never in the plan.

409	  read still valid under these rules, never from memory.
410	- *Batch only what is independent*: calls that do not depend on each other's results go in one
411	  message; never two Edits on the same file, nor a write with what must see it. Batching changes only
412	  how the same necessary operations travel: never fewer searches, reads or checks to save turns.
413	- The reviewers still read everything they need from scratch: this rule is about your own repeated
414	  reads, not theirs.
415	
416	**Optional dynamic check of DB assumptions (remote verification).** First, parse `$ARGUMENTS`: if it contains
417	`--no-dev` (or "review veloce" / "senza DEV"), skip this check entirely. Otherwise, when the plan
418	asserts facts about real data/schema (a column is nullable, an enum's values, a row's
419	existence/cardinality), verify them with a read-only query of the declared remote verification (`verifica_remota` in `.claude/maat.json`) instead of
420	deducing them statically, and feed the result into the plan/review. This runs ONLY when the plan makes
421	such a DB assertion (no assertion → nothing to run, no DEV roundtrip). `spec-plan-reviewer` stays a
422	static `Read/Grep/Glob` agent — it does NOT get Bash; the verification is this separate step.
423	
424	### How to revise: surgically, never by rewriting
425	
426	Apply each blocking finding as **one minimal, localized Edit**. Do not rewrite the section, do
427	not reorganize "while you are in there", and **do not touch a code block inside the plan unless
428	the finding is about that block**. This is the single rule that attacks the round multiplier
429	head-on: nine specs record that their late-round blockers were introduced by the previous
430	round's own revision. If a finding genuinely requires restructuring, do it — and flag that block
431	so the next round reviews it in full.
432	
433	**Measure every list you write.** Any list or count of `file:line`, occurrences or consumers that a
434	revision writes comes from a search run **just before** writing it — never from memory or from
435	the finding's text. Measured on `spec-restyling-ui-soft`: 3 of the 4 blockers raised against
436	revisions were lists of points written by inference, and "the total still adds up" hid the error

# Plan author — how the plan is written and revised

Read by whoever writes the plan section: the `plan-review-cycle` session itself for the initial plan (skeleton
first, then the full plan), and the fresh author sub-agent it launches for each format-2 revision («How to
revise»). The orchestrator keeps the finding table and the recurrence. Structure, boundaries and
differences are checked by `plan-check.sh` (`lint`, `lint2`, `skeleton`): run `lint` and, in format 2, `lint2` after
writing, and fix every `VIOLAZIONE` before you hand back.

## Single writable artifact: the spec file

This workflow writes to **exactly one file**: the specification file
`.claude/.ai-workflow/spec-<name>.md`. The plan lives **inside** it as a dedicated section.
No other files are created or modified (no `plan-<name>.md`, no `spec.md`, no versioned
files, no state file).

The spec file has this shape (spec sections authored by `spec-author` or by you when a spec
file does not yet exist; the plan section is owned by this skill):

```text
# <Title>
## Context ...
## Functional requirements ...
...spec sections...

## Implementation plan             ← OWNED by this skill
Plan format: 2                                    ← new plans only (see "Plan format 2")
Plan status: DRAFT | APPROVED | NEEDS HUMAN DECISION
Test level: min | std | full
Risk surfaces: <vocabulary tokens («Risk surfaces»), or: none>
Approved basis: spec <fp12> · plan <fp12>        ← written at approval only (Step 3); format 2: the
                                                    driver appends " · tests <fp12>" when test-red closes OK
<plan content, incl. ### Requirement traceability and ### Test plan>
### Plan review changelog
<blocker/major finding → change applied · rejected findings · optional notes · metric line>
```

**Languages (Maat 1.3.0).** Write every heading, status line, keyword and table word in the English form shown in
this file. Maat also reads the Italian forms of the same table (specs and approved plans written before 1.3.0:
`## Piano di implementazione`, `### Piano di test`, `Superfici a rischio:`, `[pavimento:`, `rosso se:`…) and never
asks to translate them. **A section that already exists keeps its heading**: re-opening or revising a plan whose
headings are Italian, you edit under those headings and keep their keywords; the English form is only for a
section you create new. Never add the English heading next to an existing Italian one: the same section in both
languages is a `plan-check.sh lint` VIOLAZIONE. An approved plan is never translated — its headings are inside the
`Approved basis:` fingerprint and it would become `STALE`.

Hard rules on writing:
- The ONLY file you may write/edit is `.claude/.ai-workflow/spec-<name>.md`.
- You may create/update ONLY the `## Implementation plan` section (`## Piano di implementazione` in an older spec)
  and its `### Plan review changelog` sub-section. **Never** modify the specification sections
  above it, and never touch any `## Implementation review` (or `## Review implementazione`) section (owned by
  `implementation-review-cycle`).
- `Plan status:` must be a **line-anchored, single-occurrence** line (downstream greps
  `^Plan status: APPROVED`). The changelog MUST NOT reproduce the literal `Plan status:`
  prefix.
- `Test level:` follows the SAME rule, and needs it more (see "Test effort"): line-anchored,
  single-occurrence, immediately under `Plan status:`. The changelog and any finding text
  quoted into the plan MUST NOT reproduce the literal `Test level:` prefix — write "livello
  di test" in prose. This matters because lens L3 now raises findings *about the test level*,
  and that text lands in the changelog.
- `Risk surfaces:` follows the SAME rule again: line-anchored, single-occurrence,
  immediately under `Test level:`; in prose write "risk surfaces" in lower case.
- **An approved plan is never edited.** After `Plan status: APPROVED` only the changelog is written
  (notes, metric line). Any other change — a new constraint, an amendment, a "small fix" — goes
  through a re-opening (SKILL.md, «re-opening»). Measured: 308 lines added to an approved plan by
  hand, once reviewed, held 1 blocker and 7 majors (`spec-restyling-ui-soft`). It is now also
  **detected**: `Approved basis:` fingerprints the spec and the plan body at approval, and
  `plan-check.sh basis` says `STALE` when either changed; `/implementation-review-cycle` and
  `/full-implementation-cycle` stop on it.

## Risk surfaces

**The risk-surface vocabulary — the single list; every other mention points here:**

| Token | Italian token (older plans) | Covers | Critical |
|---|---|---|---|
| `permissions` | `permessi` | authentication, authorization, roles, visibility by role | **yes** |
| `data` | `dati` | DB schema, migrations, persistent state, data written or deleted in bulk | **yes** |
| `destructive` | `distruttiva` | an operation that deletes or overwrites data/state irreversibly | **yes** |
| `api-contract` | `contratto-api` | request/response shape, status codes, routes consumed by others | no |
| `import` | `import` | the import pipelines | no |
| `shared-logic` | `logica-condivisa` | shared business logic, shared components/stores/composables | no |

The plan declares the touched ones in `Risk surfaces:` — bare tokens separated by commas,
or `none`; no notes on that line (`plan-check.sh lint` rejects an unknown token). The two columns are the same
token: `plan-check.sh` maps the English one to the Italian one, and prints the Italian one (`Pavimento: permessi`). **Critical** surfaces drive two things and nothing else: the verification floor
(see "Test effort") and the fresh-eyes gate after a round-1 approval (Step 2-ter). No
LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH grading: no behaviour needs it. Lens L1 verifies the declaration like any
`no implication` — under-declaring would silently skip both.

## Test effort: `--tests=min|std|full`

Parse `$ARGUMENTS` for `--tests=min|std|full`. Italian aliases count as the flag: "test minimi" /
"solo i gate" → `min`; "test completi" / "tutti i test" → `full`. **Default: `std`.**

Write the resolved level into the plan as `Test level: <lvl>`, immediately under `Plan status:`
(single occurrence, line-anchored — see the hard rules above). This line is how
`/implementation-review-cycle` learns the level; it is the only channel.

| | `min` | `std` (default) | `full` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Suite | existing gates of the **touched modules only** | same | modules' suites + lint (the CI's gates; build only if the plan prescribes it) |
| New test cases in the plan | **0**, unless a bug regression (1 case) | **≤5**, only on the behavior the plan changes | no cap |
| `[floor:` line per declared critical surface | 1, outside the caps | 1, outside the caps | 1, outside the caps |
| Counterproof (the file(s) it names reverted to base, or a named mutation; expected red) | none | on the **central gate** only (1, max 2) | every new case |
| e2e prescribed in the plan | only `[e2e-locator:` (below) | only `[e2e-locator:` (below) | at most 1 targeted spec, plus `[e2e-locator:` |
| `/browser-qa` | never | never | **never** — explicit request only |
| Length of `### Test plan` (a signal, never a finding by itself) | ~1 line | ~15 lines | free |

**A whole-suite gate is permitted but never required at `full`; it is forbidden at `min` and
`std`.** This is the criterion L3 uses to decide whether a gate is over-testing, so it must be
unambiguous.

**Section name.** The canonical heading is `### Test plan` (numbering optional, e.g.
`### 9. Test plan`; `### Piano di test` in an older plan, kept as it is). The length rule targets this heading.
Plan headings and keywords are written in English as shown here (`### Requirement traceability`, `red if:`…),
whatever the language of the prose — see «Languages» above for the sections that already exist.

**The length is measured, not enforced.** `plan-check.sh lint` prints an `AVVISO` above it; a
reviewer never raises a blocker/major on the line count alone — what blocks is what the lines
prescribe (a case over the level's cap, a duplicate, a whole suite below `full`). Measured: a major
"over the 15-line cap" cost a round and was resolved by merging lines, not by removing a test.

**Risk surfaces do NOT raise the level — but a critical one gets a floor.** The level is the
verification *budget*; it never turns `min` into `full`. Yet at `min` a permission change could
otherwise reach approval with no verification of the permission at all. So, for **each critical
surface declared** (`permissions`, `data`, `destructive` — vocabulary in «Risk surfaces»), `### Test plan`
names **exactly one** pertinent verification, as a list item of its own, marked:

```text
- [floor: permissions] <an existing test cited by path, OR 1 new case, OR a read-only DB check of the declared remote verification> red if: <condition>
```

- for `permissions`, the pertinent verification is the **negative** one (the denied role is denied);
- a `[floor:` line (`[pavimento:` in an older plan) is **exempt** from the level's caps (new cases, `### Test plan` length),
  from the L3 over-testing rule and from the "do NOT re-add" list — at most one per critical
  surface, which `plan-check.sh lint` enforces;
- if no pertinent verification is reachable, the plan writes the old **one line** instead —
  `⚠️ Surface <token> not covered by the gates at level <lvl>`, with the vocabulary token right
  after `Surface` (a `⚠️` line about another surface does not cover this one) — and continues.
  One line, not a paragraph, and outside the caps too. **Downstream it is an obligation**: the
  feature cannot reach `IMPLEMENTED` until the user reports a verification of that surface — i.e.
  in `/full-implementation-cycle` a `⚠️` on a critical surface **is a human STOP**. That is the
  honest reading of "no gate can cover it"; before, it came out `VERIFIED` with nothing having
  touched the surface at runtime. So look hard for a floor first;
- **the waiver**: when the change does not alter the surface's runtime behaviour at all (a rename,
  a message, a refactor that leaves the check itself untouched), append on the **same physical
  line** `— static sufficient: <reason>`. Then no obligation arises downstream; the surface stays
  a risk focus. L3 judges the motive: a waiver on a change that does alter the behaviour is
  under-testing. After approval the line is frozen (`Approved basis:`);
- non-critical surfaces (`api-contract`, `shared-logic`, `import`) get no floor and no
  obligation: their risk is blast radius, which is L1/L2's job, not a test's. A `⚠️` line on them
  is only a risk focus.

**Every new test case states `red if: <condition>`** — the world in which it goes red. One
clause per case, no new cap: it makes L3's non-vacuity check checkable instead of inferred.

**A counterproof names the file(s) it touches** — either reverted to the base, or a **named
mutation** (file · symbol · what is removed, e.g. "remove the `!= ROLE_MANAGER` condition in
`resolve_membership()`") — then the expected red. Use the mutation when the test imports something
the feature adds: a file back at base then fails on the import, not on the assertion (measured,
`spec-golas-obiettivo-aziendale`: an ImportError, a FAIL, a round and a human decision). Never
"revert the whole feature" nor a `git stash`: `/full-implementation-cycle` touches only the files a
gate names and records a gate that names none as `NOT RUN` — a STOP.

**An e2e bound to a locator, at any level.** When the plan changes a file in `e2e/specs/`, or a
string, class or attribute that an e2e spec uses as a locator (L3 searches every changed string
there), `### Test plan` carries one list item per affected spec:

```text
- [e2e-locator: e2e-6-customer.spec.ts] <the locator or string that changes> red if: <condition>
```

At most 2 such lines; beyond that, one `⚠️` line and the regression watch. They are outside the
level's caps like a `[floor:` line (`plan-check.sh lint` does not count them, the
`Approved basis:`
fingerprint freezes them), and downstream each is a required gate: the declared remote verification (`verifica_remota` in `.claude/maat.json`) with `--e2e <spec>` on DEV, so with
`--no-dev` the feature stops at `NEEDS_VERIFICATION` — on purpose. Measured: unit tests green while the real DOM broke a locator (`spec-partita-iva-unica-context`), and a selector changed at `std` whose e2e never ran (`spec-opzioni-offerta-salvataggio`).

**`/browser-qa` is never prescribed in a plan**, at any level: it is a separate flow, invoked by
hand when needed (and it stays a mandatory gate only at the porting cutover).

**Downstream contract — these lines are consumed, not just read.** `/implementation-review-cycle`
parses the approved plan with `plan-check.sh contract` and does NOT re-derive what the plan already
decided:
- every gate written in `### Test plan` becomes a **required gate** of the implementation
  review (a feature cannot reach `IMPLEMENTED` until it has passed on the reviewed code). So write
  each gate as something that can be executed and observed — a test file, a command, a counterproof
  with its expected red — never as a wish ("verify that it works");
- every `⚠️ Surface <token> not covered…` line becomes a **risk focus** the implementation reviewer
  must look at first: keep it to the surfaces that are really uncovered;
- the surfaces of `Risk surfaces:` are a risk focus too, a `[floor:` or `[e2e-locator:`
  line is a required gate like any other, a critical surface with neither a floor nor a waiver is an
  **obligation** closed only by the user's evidence, and `### Requirement traceability` is the
  requirement list the implementation reviewer reports coverage against.
Over-prescribing here therefore costs twice: once in the plan, once as a gate that must pass.

## Plan format 2

A plan whose section opens with the line `Plan format: 2` — right under `## Implementation plan`,
above `Plan status:`, line-anchored, single occurrence — is in **format 2**. **Every plan this skill
writes from scratch is in format 2.** A plan without the line is **format 1** and follows the rest of
this file exactly as before — a format-1 plan re-opened later included: it is never converted.
Everything above (status lines, level, surfaces, floors, `red if:`, `Approved basis:`) holds in both.

**Structure.** H3 sections (numbering optional); the table headers are fixed — `plan-check.sh` reads
them:

```text
## Implementation plan
Plan format: 2
Plan status: DRAFT
Test level: std
Risk surfaces: permissions, api-contract

### Decisions
<one short paragraph per decision, then its examples>
| input | output |
|---|---|
| target €1,000,000, assigned €950,000 | `near` (boundary: remainder = threshold) |

### Touched files
- `backend/app/routers/goals.py`
- `backend/tests/test_goals.py`

### Steps
#### Block B1 — backend
writes: `backend/app/routers/goals.py`, `backend/tests/test_goals.py`
after: none

| id | file | change | test |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | `backend/app/routers/goals.py` | `update_goal()`: 403 for whoever cannot edit | T1 |

#### Block B2 — frontend
writes: `frontend/components/goals/PlanTable.vue`
after: B1

### Requirement traceability
| Req | Plan steps | Verification |
|---|---|---|
| FR1 | P1 | T1 |
| FR2 | P2 | not verifiable by a test: <reason> |

### Strings and data-test
| action | type | value |
|---|---|---|
| removes | data-test | `goals-company-section` |
| adds | string | `Edit company goal` |

### Test plan
| ID | requirement | file | assertion | mutation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | FR1 | `backend/tests/test_goals.py::test_update_denied` (new) | red if: a salesperson updates the target | `backend/app/routers/goals.py` · `update_goal` · `if not can_edit:` → `if False:` · red if: `assert 200 == 403` |
- [floor: permissions] T1
```

The Italian forms of an older format-2 plan, kept where the section already exists: `## Piano di implementazione`,
`### Decisioni` · `### File toccati` · `### Passi` · `### Tracciabilità requisiti` · `### Stringhe e data-test` ·
`### Piano di test`, `#### Blocco <id>` with `scrive:` / `dopo:` (`nessuno`), the headers `id | file | modifica |
test`, `azione | tipo | valore` (`aggiunge` / `toglie`, `stringa` / `data-test`, column `verificato`),
`ID | requisito | file | asserzione | mutazione`, `rosso se:`, `(vuoto)`, `(nuovo)`, `[pavimento: <token>]`,
`⚠️ Rischio aperto`. Each reader accepts both.

- **Paths** are relative to the repository, everywhere (their first segment exists at the root).
- **New files**: in `### Touched files`, `(new)` right after the path's code span (`` - `path` (new) ``)
  marks a file the plan creates. Downstream (harness-pt11) it is the `test-red` phase's write scope with the
  test files, where the stubs of the new symbols go, and the only kind of file whose counterproof can be
  absorbed (L2).
- **Acceptance tests (test-red)**: every row of `### Test plan` is written and proven red on the base with
  stubs before the implementation. The red must hit the row's assertion, at a position in the test file: put
  the expected failure text between backticks in `assertion` (else the mutation's `red if:` is used) — a row
  with neither is a `lint2` VIOLATION, and a red with no text or no position is not proven; every string or `data-test` the plan
  adds must be listed as `adds` in `### Strings and data-test` — an existing test asserting its absence is
  a conflict that stops the phase.
- **Stubs go only into new files.** A new parameter (or an extra positional argument) of a function that already
  exists gets no signature stub: on the base the test fails with the `TypeError` of the call, before its assertion.
  Its red is that one — `` red if: `unexpected keyword argument 'sep'` `` (or `` `positional argument` ``) — not the
  value the implementation will return; the mutation's `red if:` keeps the value (it runs on the implemented code).
  `lint2` gives a VIOLATION when a Python call in the row's backticks does not fit the signature of an existing
  function of `### Touched files` and the row's red does not name the `TypeError`.
- **Reports.** The test-red phase reads the outcome of each test from the module's report (`report: junit` or
  `vitest` in `.claude/maat.json`): a row in a module with `report: nessuno` gets a `lint2` AVVISO, because the phase
  would stop BLOCKED. It is configuration, not plan: say it to the user in the round's summary, do not rewrite the plan
  for it.
- **Decisions** stay prose; the input → output examples are what the implementer and the tests read.
- **Steps**: every step is a row `id | file | change | test` inside a `#### Block <id>`; each block
  declares `writes:` (the files it writes) and `after:` (the blocks it depends on, or `none`).
- **Test plan**: one row per case. `file` = the test, as the first code span: `path` or
  `path::name` (pytest node id, or vitest full name — required when the row has a mutation; a Python class and
  its method are separated by `::` even for `unittest` tests: `test_x.py::TestX::test_y`, never `TestX.test_y`,
  a `lint2` VIOLATION; a pytest doctest id keeps its dots: `mod.py::mod.func`); `(new)`
  after the span marks a new case, the one the level's caps count. `assertion` = the case's
  `red if:`. `requirement` = the IDs of `### Requirement traceability` it verifies.
- **Existing non-regression tests are NOT rows of `### Test plan`.** A test that already exists and must
  only stay green («stays green», «remains green», «keeps passing» — or the Italian «resta verde», «rimane verde»,
  «continua a passare») cannot be proven red on the base with stubs, so as a row it stops the cycle at test-red —
  `lint2` gives a VIOLATION for a row whose `assertion` starts that way. Put them in a note right under the table,
  one item each: «EXISTING non-regression tests (not rows of the Test plan: they cannot be proven red on the base
  with stubs):» — `path` (or `path::name`), what stays true, the requirement IDs, and the explicit command when the
  test is outside the gate of the touched modules. A requirement covered only by such a test is written in
  `### Requirement traceability` as ``not verifiable by a test (invariance, cannot be proven red): covered by the
  existing test `<path>` `` (the `not verifiable` prefix — or `non verificabile` — is what `lint2` accepts); the
  step's `test` column then names no ID for it (`—`). A test the plan **updates** is not «stays green»: it is a row
  with its `red if:`.
- **mutation** = the counterproof, in `counterproof.sh`'s form, or `—`:
  `` `file` · `symbol` · `search` → `replace` · red if: `text of the error message` ``.
  `(empty)` in place of the replacement removes `search`; `search` must occur **once** in the file
  *after* the implementation; a `|` is written `\|`, a backtick needs a double-backtick span. File and
  test in the same module of `.claude/maat.json` (a test under the `radice` of the file's module). Which rows
  carry one follows the level (none at `min`, the central gate at `std`, every new case at `full`).
- `[floor:`, `[e2e-locator:` and `⚠️` lines stay list items under the table, as in format 1; a
  floor that is a row of the table names its ID.
- **Strings and data-test**: every string or `data-test` the plan removes (`removes`) or adds (`adds`).
  `lint2` searches the existing tests for them and decides, by the literal's position, whether a match asserts
  presence (a `VIOLAZIONE` unless the file is one the plan touches — an e2e spec: its `[e2e-locator:` line) or
  absence (an `AVVISO`). An optional fourth column `verified` — `` `<file>` — <reason> `` — waives that row's
  match in that file: `| removes | string | `Active` | `frontend/tests/x.test.ts` — rewritten by flow X |`.
- **A product defect found late** (round 3 or 4) does not reopen the design: it becomes one test row, with its
  step, and one list item `⚠️ Open risk: <claim> — <test ID>` under the table.

**Generated, never written.** The plan carries **no** command line, no `test-fast.sh` path list, no
pytest selector, no counterproof recipe: `plan-check.sh gen <spec>` derives them from the test table and
writes them to the run directory — `<spec>.run/gen/procedura.txt` (level, commands, paths, blocks) and
`<spec>.run/counterproof/mutations.json` (the list `counterproof.sh` reads; removed when no row has a
mutation). A procedure written by hand cannot be wrong, because there is none.

## Skeleton first (format 2)

A plan too large does not converge (the reviewers sample it instead of exhausting it). Asked for the skeleton:
1. **Skeleton first.** Write only the skeleton into the plan section: `Plan format: 2` and the status lines
   (`Plan status: DRAFT`), `### Touched files`, and `### Steps` with its `#### Block` blocks and one row per
   step (`| id | file | change | test |` — a few words in `change`, `test` may be `—`). No decisions, no
   traceability, no test plan yet. Then `plan-check.sh skeleton <spec>`:
   - `Scheletro: SOTTO IL TETTO` (≤15 steps, ≤40 files) → write the full plan **starting from the skeleton**
     (it is its backbone: nothing is thrown away);
   - `Scheletro: SOPRA IL TETTO` (exit 1) → **cut proposal** (below).
   The orchestrator runs `plan-check.sh skeleton` (ceilings in its constants: ≤15 steps, ≤40 files, a full plan
   ≤400 lines) and, under them, asks for the full plan **starting from the skeleton** (nothing is thrown away).

## Writing the plan

Analyze the local codebase and write the `## Implementation plan` section into
`.claude/.ai-workflow/spec-<name>.md` with `Plan status: DRAFT`, `Test level: <lvl>` and
`Risk surfaces: <tokens | none>`. Copy the spec to the scratchpad **before** writing
(the `lint` baseline), and after writing run `plan-check.sh lint <spec> --baseline <copy>`.

**`### Requirement traceability`** — one row per requirement, with the ID as the spec writes it
(`FR1`, `RF1` in an older spec, `D3`, `Requirement A`…) or `FR<n>` by position when the spec has none. Cite the
spec's ids literally: `RF1` and `FR1` are **different** ids (no alias), and a chain ring uses its mother's family:

```text
| Req | Plan steps | Verification |
| FR1 | 2, 3 | test_x.py::test_y · or: not verifiable by a test, <reason> |
```

One row each, no prose: a small feature gets a three-row table. L1 checks it (not a script: real
specs number requirements in too many ways for a count to be reliable).

The plan must cover: objective; relevant files/components/stores/services/routes/tests/
APIs; current behavior; proposed behavior; implementation steps; data-flow implications;
UI implications; backend implications; validation rules; permission rules; migration/
persistence implications; risks; requirement traceability (below); test plan **at the declared
level** (see "Test effort"); rollback considerations; explicit out-of-scope.

**Size the plan to the change — these sections are conditional, not mandatory prose.**
A section with nothing to say gets **one line, `no implication`** — never a paragraph of
filler. Measured: plans average ~700 lines and reach 1314, and that volume is the surface every
round rewrites, which is where self-inflicted defects come from. An explicit `no
implication` is a verifiable claim; filler prose is indistinguishable from real content, to a
human reader and to a reviewer alike.

Lens **L1** is required to check every one of those declarations, so writing one without
looking will be caught.

# Spec: split the argument parser into small internal modules, with no change of behaviour

## Context

The whole package is one file, `index.js`: a single exported function of about 250 lines that contains, as inner
or top-level helpers, the number test (`isNumber`), the nested-key lookup (`hasKey`), the nested-key assignment with
its prototype-pollution protections (`setKey`) and the normalisation of the options into flags and aliases. These
pieces cannot be read or tested on their own.

The package supports very old Node versions (`"engines": { "node": ">= 0.4" }` in `package.json`), so its code is
written in ES5 (`var`, function expressions, no arrow functions, no `let`/`const`, no template literals, no
spread). Its tests use `tape` and live in `test/*.js` (`npx tape 'test/**/*.js'`); the lint is
`npx eslint --ext=js,mjs .` with the configuration in `.eslintrc` (a strict shared configuration: for example it
allows at most three parameters per function and requires sorted object keys).

## Goal

The same package, with the same behaviour for every input, whose helpers live in separate modules under `lib/`
with their own unit tests.

## Functional requirements

FR1. Behaviour does not change: for every `args` array and every `opts` object, `require('minimist')(args, opts)`
returns a result deeply equal to the one returned before the change (same keys, same values, same types, same
order of the `_` and `--` arrays), and calls `opts.unknown` with the same arguments, in the same order, the same
number of times. This includes the existing protections against prototype pollution (`__proto__`, `constructor`,
the built-in prototypes).

FR2. New CommonJS modules, each exporting a single function as `module.exports`, in strict mode:
- FR2.1 `lib/is-number.js` exports `isNumber(x)`, with exactly the semantics of today's `isNumber` in `index.js`.
- FR2.2 `lib/has-key.js` exports `hasKey(obj, keys)`, with exactly the semantics of today's `hasKey`.
- FR2.3 `lib/set-key.js` exports `createSetKey(isBooleanKey)`, which returns a function
  `setKey(obj, keys, value)` with exactly the semantics of today's `setKey`, where the boolean-key test it uses
  is the `isBooleanKey` function given to `createSetKey` (`isBooleanKey(key)` returns a boolean). It keeps every
  prototype-pollution protection of today's code.
- FR2.4 `lib/build-flags.js` exports `buildFlags(opts)`, which returns a new object with these properties,
  computed from `opts` exactly as `index.js` computes them today: `bools` (object: key → `true`), `strings`
  (object: key → `true`, aliases included), `allBools` (`true` when `opts.boolean === true`, `false` otherwise),
  `unknownFn` (the `opts.unknown` function, or `null`), `aliases` (object: each name → array of its other names).
  `buildFlags(undefined)` behaves as `buildFlags({})`.

FR3. `index.js` keeps exporting the parser function as `module.exports` and uses the four modules of FR2: it no
longer defines its own `isNumber`, `hasKey`, `setKey` or the code that builds flags and aliases. The argument loop
stays in `index.js`.

FR4. Each module of FR2 has unit tests in a new file `test/lib-<module name>.js` (for example
`test/lib-set-key.js`), written with `tape` like the existing tests. The existing files in `test/` are not modified.

FR5. All JavaScript files of the package, new and changed, are ES5 and pass the project's lint.

FR6. The new modules are part of the published package: `npm pack --dry-run` lists `lib/is-number.js`,
`lib/has-key.js`, `lib/set-key.js` and `lib/build-flags.js`.

## Codebase areas involved (indicative)

- `index.js`.
- `test/` (existing tests, unchanged; new `test/lib-*.js`).
- `package.json`, `.eslintrc` (read; change only if needed for FR6 or the lint).

AC1. The existing test suite passes unchanged: `npx tape 'test/**/*.js'`.

AC2. The output and the `opts.unknown` calls of the new `index.js` are identical to those of the old one over a
large generated set of argument lists and option objects (booleans, strings, aliases, defaults, dotted keys,

- "Exactly the semantics of today's code" includes its quirks: a quirk is preserved, not fixed.

- Any change of behaviour, including fixing bugs found along the way (report them instead).
- Performance work, new options, TypeScript types, a changelog entry (the changelog is generated at release).
- New runtime dependencies. New development dependencies are not needed either.

## Constraints

- ES5 syntax and CommonJS, as the rest of the package (`engines.node >= 0.4`).
- The project's lint configuration is not relaxed to make the new code pass.

12	  section (format 2: `Plan format: 2`). A plan written before Maat 1.3.0 has the Italian headings and keywords

21	  still under its final gate).

24	
25	1. **One test per row of `### Test plan`**, in the file of its `file` column, with the name of its
26	   `path::name` (pytest node id, vitest full name — `describe` titles and the `it` title joined by spaces).
27	   - The test asserts the row's `assertion`. When that column has a text between backticks (or the row has a
28	     mutation with `red if:`), that text must appear in the failure message **on the base with stubs**:
29	     the driver checks it.
30	   - A row in an **existing** test file: add the case, never change or delete the cases already there.
31	   - Follow the conventions of the neighbouring tests (imports, fixtures, `mountSuspended`, factories).
32	2. **One stub per new symbol** the plan names, in the new files of the scope: the **exported signature**
33	   exactly as the plan and its `### Decisions` examples describe it, and a body that **does not** satisfy
34	   the assertion (`return ''`, `return 0`, `return null`, `raise NotImplementedError` only if the test
35	   checks a value and not the exception). A stub is never the implementation, not even partly.
36	   - Export **every** new symbol a test imports, and nothing else: an import that does not resolve is a red
37	     that proves nothing (the driver calls it «not proven» (Italian: «non dimostrato») and stops the phase).
38	   - Every exported symbol of a new file must be used by at least one acceptance test.
39	   - A function that **already exists** gets no stub, not even of its signature: a test of its new parameter fails

41	     argument …`). If the row's red holds only with a signature stub, it is a deviation of the plan: say so.

50	  (first line: the folder to run it from, relative to the repository, `.` = the repository; second line: the

     mutation with `red if:`), that text must appear in the failure message **on the base with stubs**:
     the driver checks it.
   - A row in an **existing** test file: add the case, never change or delete the cases already there.
   - Follow the conventions of the neighbouring tests (imports, fixtures, `mountSuspended`, factories).
2. **One stub per new symbol** the plan names, in the new files of the scope: the **exported signature**
   exactly as the plan and its `### Decisions` examples describe it, and a body that **does not** satisfy
   the assertion (`return ''`, `return 0`, `return null`, `raise NotImplementedError` only if the test
   checks a value and not the exception). A stub is never the implementation, not even partly.
   - Export **every** new symbol a test imports, and nothing else: an import that does not resolve is a red
     that proves nothing (the driver calls it «not proven» (Italian: «non dimostrato») and stops the phase).
   - Every exported symbol of a new file must be used by at least one acceptance test.
   - A function that **already exists** gets no stub, not even of its signature: a test of its new parameter fails
     on the base with the `TypeError` of the call, and that is the red the plan declares (`unexpected keyword
     argument …`). If the row's red holds only with a signature stub, it is a deviation of the plan: say so.
3. Nothing else: no production code outside the stubs, no fixtures elsewhere, no snapshot files.

## Inner loop

Run **only the files you wrote**, targeted (the guard denies full suites):
- every module: its test command declared in `.claude/maat.json`, on your test file, with the interpreter and in
  the environment the gates use. Print it with
  `. "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/python.sh" && "$FIC_PY" "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/maat-config.py" comando <module> test --test <test file relative to the repository>`
  (first line: the folder to run it from, relative to the repository, `.` = the repository; second line: the
  command, `{python}` already resolved — the interpreter alone is `… maat-config.py python <module>`; add
  `--report <a file outside the repository>` when the command has `{report}`). With `ambiente: wsl` run it inside
  WSL (`wsl -- bash -lc 'cd /mnt/<drive>/<repo>/<folder> && <command>'`, a `C:/…` interpreter written `/mnt/c/…`):
  that is the one with the production versions. Never another interpreter that happens to be at hand (e.g. a
  Windows venv next to the WSL one): it may answer differently from production (e.g. 401 instead of 403). No such
  interpreter → `BLOCKED (venv assente)`.

Every acceptance test must be **red on its assertion**, not on an import or a collection error. A test
that is **green** on the base proves nothing: stop and report it (the plan asserts something the code
already does, or the test is wrong). If an existing test in the same run turns red, or the plan's
assertion contradicts a test already in the repository, **stop**: that is a contradiction of the plan,
and correcting acceptance tests or the plan is a human decision. `test-stage` does not run tests: the
driver verifies the staged tests after the plan is approved.

The final verification is the driver's (`run-phase.sh`: `gates.sh` targeted, then `plan-check.sh rossi`
on the evidence); your inner loop only avoids handing it an obvious failure.

## Hard bans

As `plan-implementer`: no remote hosts, no database writes, no docker, no git state changes, no package
installs, never the spec file, never a file outside the scope.

## Report — always this shape

```text
Result: COMPLETED | PARTIAL | DEVIATION
Mode: test-red | test-stage
Tests written:
- <ID> — <file>::<name> — red on: <failure text observed, or "non eseguito (test-stage)">

- <file> — <exported symbols>

- <command> → <FAIL (expected) | PASS | BLOCKED> — <last lines of the REAL output>
```

# Spec: split the argument parser into small internal modules, with no change of behaviour

## Context

The whole package is one file, `index.js`: a single exported function of about 250 lines that contains, as inner
or top-level helpers, the number test (`isNumber`), the nested-key lookup (`hasKey`), the nested-key assignment with
its prototype-pollution protections (`setKey`) and the normalisation of the options into flags and aliases. These
pieces cannot be read or tested on their own.

The package supports very old Node versions (`"engines": { "node": ">= 0.4" }` in `package.json`), so its code is
written in ES5 (`var`, function expressions, no arrow functions, no `let`/`const`, no template literals, no
spread). Its tests use `tape` and live in `test/*.js` (`npx tape 'test/**/*.js'`); the lint is
`npx eslint --ext=js,mjs .` with the configuration in `.eslintrc` (a strict shared configuration: for example it
allows at most three parameters per function and requires sorted object keys).

The same package, with the same behaviour for every input, whose helpers live in separate modules under `lib/`
with their own unit tests.

## Functional requirements

FR1. Behaviour does not change: for every `args` array and every `opts` object, `require('minimist')(args, opts)`
returns a result deeply equal to the one returned before the change (same keys, same values, same types, same
order of the `_` and `--` arrays), and calls `opts.unknown` with the same arguments, in the same order, the same
number of times. This includes the existing protections against prototype pollution (`__proto__`, `constructor`,

- FR2.1 `lib/is-number.js` exports `isNumber(x)`, with exactly the semantics of today's `isNumber` in `index.js`.

- FR2.3 `lib/set-key.js` exports `createSetKey(isBooleanKey)`, which returns a function
  `setKey(obj, keys, value)` with exactly the semantics of today's `setKey`, where the boolean-key test it uses
  is the `isBooleanKey` function given to `createSetKey` (`isBooleanKey(key)` returns a boolean). It keeps every
  prototype-pollution protection of today's code.

  computed from `opts` exactly as `index.js` computes them today: `bools` (object: key → `true`), `strings`

`lib/has-key.js`, `lib/set-key.js` and `lib/build-flags.js`.

large generated set of argument lists and option objects (booleans, strings, aliases, defaults, dotted keys,

AC4. `npx eslint --ext=js,mjs .` passes; every `.js` file of the package parses as ECMAScript 5.

- "Exactly the semantics of today's code" includes its quirks: a quirk is preserved, not fixed.

- Any change of behaviour, including fixing bugs found along the way (report them instead).
- Performance work, new options, TypeScript types, a changelog entry (the changelog is generated at release).
